limitations: Current user rules: P0 (maximum severity) for any multiple-choice prompt, including explicit binary choices, and any answer list with more than one entry—even equivalent spellings, capitalization variants or number/word aliases. Prior suggestions to add or retain aliases are superseded: keep one canonical answer only. Existing finding IDs remain stable; new format findings have new IDs.
All 41 supplied YAML files parsed successfully. YAML nodes were inspected before mapping construction, preserving duplicate keys and their line numbers.

All entries were included in structural screening and text/answer-label review. This is an editorial audit with selective external fact-checking, not independent source verification of all 10,956 answers.

Fact-check candidates are proposed concerns and corrections awaiting authoritative verification. They are not confirmed errors. Editorial findings may combine language fixes with an unsourced factual suggestion; verify that component before applying it.

Inventory cards display original answers alongside recorded findings and proposed actions. Original answers have not been corrected. No linked image was visually certified. Six attempted image retrievals (Minnesota, Utah, Mississippi, Kyrgyzstan, Syria and one Pokémon sample) were blocked by the browsing tool. This does not establish that those URLs are dead. All 1,563 image-dependent rows remain visually unverified.

Bot source and runtime were not inspected. Boolean coercion is demonstrated by PyYAML; actual behavior depends on the bot loader. Answer-alias redundancy assumes case/punctuation/accent normalization and is therefore conditional.

Exact text duplicates, normalized text matches, semantic repetition and inverse questions are different. Cross-category repeats and state↔abbreviation inverse pairs may be intentional. Do not delete them indiscriminately.
Absence of a flag means no issue was recorded in this pass, not a guarantee that an answer is correct. Original YAML files were not modified. Line numbers refer to the copied source snapshot.
pack_notes: U.S. abbreviation pack contains the 50 standard USPS state pairs in both directions; no answer mismatch observed. Clarify “two-letter USPS abbreviation” in the forward prompts. These inverse pairs are intentional practice, not automatic duplicates.

U.S. flags/maps each contain 55 labels (50 states plus five inhabited territories). Neither includes Washington, D.C.; this is a scope choice because D.C. is a federal district, not a state or territory.

World flag/map packs have different 196-label inventories: flags include Palestine and Western Sahara where maps include Chad and Indonesia. Normalize an explicit country/territory coverage policy. This is an inventory difference, not proof that either image is mislabeled.

The nine Pokémon image packs contain 1,025 entries in total. The first eight contain 905; generation-nine sprite filenames run 906–1025. Numeric filenames reveal Pokédex identifiers if visible to players. Species labels do not certify the opaque image mappings.
Flag refresh priorities include Minnesota, Utah, Mississippi, Mauritania, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan and Syria. Date/context matters; historical flags can remain valid if explicitly labeled.
Slogans should be treated as historical campaigns. Old slogans are not wrong merely because a brand now uses another slogan; specify country/campaign/year when ambiguous.
Sports records and sponsorship names need fixed season cutoffs. Fiction questions need book/film/anime adaptation, game release, localization or generation when answers differ.
